quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: U.S. FDA grants Priority Review for Roche's Enspryng for (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA granted Priority Review to the supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for Enspryng (satralizumab) in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), a disease with no approved treatments; the FDA decision is expected by 10 January 2027. It is Enspryng's second FDA Priority Review, after thyroid eye disease (TED) in June 2026. The EMA has validated the EU application, with a European Commission decision expected in the third quarter of 2027. The filing rests on the Phase III METEOROID study: Enspryng reduced the risk of a new relapse by 68% versus placebo (p=0.0025), with 87% of treated patients relapse-free at 48 weeks versus 67% on placebo, plus significant improvements in annualised relapse rate, MRI lesion activity and rescue therapy use. If approved, Enspryng would be the first and only disease-modifying therapy for MOGAD (company claim).
